purpose: Lets a user choose exactly one option from a small, fixed list where all options should be visible at once. Use when choices are mutually exclusive and there are between two and five options. For six or more options, use Select. For choices that are not mutually exclusive, use Checkbox.

props.name: legend
props.description: Labels the whole group. Rendered as a <legend> inside a <fieldset> so screen readers announce it before each option.

props.name: name
props.description: Ties all Radio inputs in the group together. Must be unique within the form. This is what enforces mutual exclusivity in HTML.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value. Pass this to control the group from outside.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new value when the user selects a different option.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: When set, puts the group into an error state and shows this message below all options.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every Radio in the group. The HTML disabled attribute on a fieldset disables all its children automatically.

props.name: children
props.description: The Radio components. Each Radio needs a label and a value.

variants.name: default
variants.whenToUse: Any time the user must pick exactly one option from two to five choices that should all be visible without interaction.

variants.name: error
variants.whenToUse: When the user has submitted without making a selection and a choice is required. Always pair with an errorMessage explaining what is needed.

states.name: unchecked
states.description: Resting state. Empty circle with strong border.

states.name: checked
states.description: Brand-coloured outer ring with filled inner dot.

states.name: focus
states.description: Keyboard focus on the active option. Visible 2px focus ring using the focus-ring token.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Non-interactive. Circle uses disabled surface and border tokens. Inner dot uses disabled text token.

states.name: error
states.description: No selection made when one is required. Error message shown below the group.

antiPatterns.never: Use RadioGroup for more than five options.
antiPatterns.because: A long list of visible radio buttons clutters the layout and makes scanning hard. Select hides the options behind a click but is the right trade-off once the list grows beyond five items.

antiPatterns.never: Use RadioGroup for choices that are not mutually exclusive.
antiPatterns.because: Radio buttons communicate that selecting one deselects all others. If the user should be able to pick more than one, use Checkboxes instead.

antiPatterns.never: Render a Radio outside a RadioGroup.
antiPatterns.because: A lone Radio has no name attribute and is not connected to any group. It will not deselect other options and its value will not be submitted correctly. Radio only makes sense as part of a group.

antiPatterns.never: Use RadioGroup for a binary yes/no when a single Checkbox would do.
antiPatterns.because: Two radios labelled Yes and No is a common pattern but usually wrong. A single checkbox communicates the same thing with less visual weight and one fewer element.

accessibility.role: radiogroup (native <fieldset> with role inferred from context)
keyboard: Tab moves focus into the group, landing on the selected option or the first option if none selected
Arrow keys (Up/Down or Left/Right) move between options within the group
Tab moves focus out of the group entirely — arrow keys handle in-group navigation
accessibility.focus: Visible 2px focus ring on :focus-visible using the focus-ring token, offset by 2px. Only the active option in the group is in the tab order at any time.
aria: fieldset and legend provide the group label — no aria-labelledby needed when this structure is used
aria-describedby on the fieldset points to the error message when errorMessage is set
Each Radio is a native <input type='radio'> — no ARIA role needed
accessibility.contrast: Brand dot on white meets WCAG AA 3:1 for UI components. Disabled dot on disabled surface meets WCAG AA 4.5:1.

agentNotes: Always use RadioGroup, never a bare Radio. The group owns the name, the legend, and the error message. The decision rule: 2–5 mutually exclusive options → RadioGroup; 6+ options → Select; non-exclusive options → Checkbox; a single boolean → Checkbox. The keyboard pattern for radio groups is different from all other controls: arrow keys navigate between options, Tab exits the group. Do not instruct the user to Tab between radio options.
